title: Add optional notes field to BenchmarkRun
body:
Target: orgos/agile/benchmark.py
Class: BenchmarkRun (@dataclass)

Add a new field: `notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)`. Place it after the `error` field. Ensure to_json() still works (no code change needed there — asdict handles it).

Verify by writing a tiny pytest at tests/agile/test_benchmark_notes.py:
  - constructing a BenchmarkRun without notes returns notes == []
  - constructing with notes=['a','b'] serialises through to_json()

Run: pytest tests/agile/test_benchmark_notes.py -v

title: takt_time must raise on negative duration
body:
Target: orgos/agile/flow_metric.py, function takt_time

Current behavior: takt_time returns 0.0 when n_issues <= 0. It does NOT check duration_seconds — a negative duration silently produces a nonsense negative takt. That's a bug.

Fix: raise ValueError('duration_seconds must be >= 0') when duration_seconds < 0. Zero and positive remain valid.

Regression test: create tests/agile/test_takt_negative.py with:
  - test_negative_duration_raises: pytest.raises(ValueError) around     takt_time(-1.0, 5)
  - test_zero_duration_ok: takt_time(0.0, 1) == 0.0
  - test_positive_duration_ok: takt_time(3600.0, 2) == 1800.0

Verify BOTH: pytest tests/agile/test_takt_negative.py -v AND pytest tests/agile/test_flow_metric.py -v (existing suite must still pass).

title: Extract cost_usd into a new pricing_util module
body:
Currently orgos/agile/pricing.py contains _PER_MILLION and cost_usd.

1. Create orgos/agile/pricing_util.py that exposes ONLY cost_usd,    importing _PER_MILLION from pricing.
2. In orgos/agile/benchmark.py and orgos/agile/solo_baseline.py,    change the import from `from orgos.agile.pricing import cost_usd`    to `from orgos.agile.pricing_util import cost_usd`.
3. Keep orgos/agile/pricing.py's cost_usd function in place for    backwards compat (do not delete it).

Verify: python -c 'from orgos.agile.benchmark import run_team' must succeed with no ImportError. Then run pytest tests/agile/ -q — the existing suite must still pass.

title: Extract flow-score tolerance constant in tests
body:
Target: tests/agile/test_flow_metric.py

Some assertions use `pytest.approx(x, abs=1e-3)` or `rel=1e-3` sprinkled inline. If any such magic tolerance appears in the file, extract it to a module-level constant FLOAT_TOL = 1e-3 at the top of the file, and reference FLOAT_TOL in the assertions.

If no magic tolerance exists in the file, add FLOAT_TOL = 1e-3 at the top with a short comment and leave the tests unchanged (this is still a valid outcome — but note that in a summary line).

Verify: pytest tests/agile/test_flow_metric.py -v must still pass.

title: Add summarize_runs helper with 5 required behaviors
body:
Add a new function to orgos/agile/benchmark.py:
  def summarize_runs(runs: list[BenchmarkRun]) -> dict:

REQUIRED BEHAVIORS (all five must be met):
  AC1. Returns a dict with keys: n, total_cost_usd, total_tokens,        avg_quality, commit_rate.
  AC2. For an empty list, returns        {'n': 0, 'total_cost_usd': 0.0, 'total_tokens': 0,         'avg_quality': None, 'commit_rate': 0.0}.
  AC3. avg_quality is the mean of all non-None quality_ac,        quality_code, quality_tests across all runs (flat mean,        not per-run mean). If none present, avg_quality is None.
  AC4. commit_rate = fraction of runs with commit_produced True.        Rounded to 3 decimal places.
  AC5. total_cost_usd rounded to 4 decimal places. total_tokens is int.

Add tests/agile/test_summarize_runs.py with one test per AC (5 tests).

Verify: pytest tests/agile/test_summarize_runs.py -v must be 5/5.

title: Add sprint_status classifier module
body:
Create NEW orgos/agile/sprint_status.py:
  from __future__ import annotations
  from orgos.agile.benchmark import BenchmarkRun

  def classify_status(run: BenchmarkRun) -> str:

Rules (evaluated in order):
  - if not run.commit_produced -> 'failed'
  - if run.tests_failed > 0 -> 'tests_failing'
  - if run.quality_ac is None or run.quality_ac < 3 -> 'poor_quality'
  - otherwise -> 'ok'

Create tests/agile/test_sprint_status.py with 4 tests, one per branch. Construct BenchmarkRun instances with the fields needed for each branch (leave others at reasonable defaults).

Verify: pytest tests/agile/test_sprint_status.py -v must be 4/4.

title: Extract baseline-SHA capture into a shared helper
body:
Both orgos/agile/sprint.py::run_pull_sprint and orgos/agile/solo_baseline.py::run_solo capture the baseline SHA the same way, right after _make_worktree:

    baseline_sha = subprocess.run(
        ['git', 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'],
        cwd=str(worktree), capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10,
    ).stdout.strip()

Extract this into a shared helper in orgos/agile/sprint.py:
    def capture_baseline_sha(worktree: Path) -> str: ...

Then update both call sites to use it. Do not change any behavior.

Verify: pytest tests/agile/ -q — the existing suite must still pass.
Also verify no ImportError: python -c 'from orgos.agile.sprint import capture_baseline_sha, run_pull_sprint; from orgos.agile.solo_baseline import run_solo'
